# craft-workflow

This is the source of the craft-workflow plugin: a cost-routed engineering
workflow for Claude Code, Codex CLI, and ZCode. If you are an agent working
in this repository, you are working on the plugin itself, not using it on an
application.

## Where things live

- `skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/` are the Claude Code source. Codex reads
  the generated mirror instead: `.agents/skills/`, `.codex/agents/`.
- ZCode reads `skills/`, `commands/`, and `hooks/` directly through
  `.zcode-plugin/plugin.json`, and reads the generated mirror
  `.zcode-plugin/agents/` for its subagents, whose model ids come from
  `ZCODE_AGENT_MODELS` in `bin/craft-sync-codex`.
- `config/workflow.md` is the one file a plugin user edits to retarget the
  workflow. Do not change routing behavior anywhere else.
- `standards/` holds the vendored engineering standards every skill and
  reviewer reads.
- `hooks/` holds the Claude Code hooks this plugin enforces, not just
  requests: the spec gate, `*.human.md` protection, the done/Gate-A check,
  and the session-start status. Codex CLI does not run them yet - see
  "Codex support" below.
- `hooks/mod/` is a Claude Code mod (`hooks/mod.json`, named by
  `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`): the status, the craft board, cost per agent.
  It enforces nothing. ZCode and Codex do not load it.
- `stacks/<id>/stack.json` are the stack packs (django, fastapi, go, java,
  node) that `bin/craft-stack` detects. `config/deciders.json` lists the AI
  deciders `bin/craft-decide` chooses from.

## Generated files - do not hand-edit

`.agents/skills/`, `.codex/agents/`, `.zcode-plugin/agents/`, and this file
(`AGENTS.md`) are generated by `bin/craft-sync-codex` from `skills/`,
`commands/`, and `agents/`. Edit the source directory, then run:

    bin/craft-sync-codex --write

Hand-editing a generated file is overwritten on the next `--write`, and
`bin/craft-sync-codex` (with no flag) reports the edit as drift.

## Codex support - what works today

Skills, commands, and subagents are available to Codex through the generated
mirror. The three hook-enforced gates - `*.human.md` protection, the spec
gate, and the done/Gate-A verification at session end - run only under
Claude Code and ZCode today. The `bin/` commands (`craft-spec`,
`craft-approve`, `craft-check`, `craft-std`) work the same under every tool.
A Codex session can still follow the same workflow as prose, but nothing
blocks it from skipping a gate the way the Claude Code hooks do. Do not tell a developer these gates are enforced under Codex until
`.codex/hooks.json` ships.

## ZCode support - what works today

Skills, commands, and subagents are available to ZCode through
`.zcode-plugin/plugin.json`, and ZCode runs the same `hooks/hooks.json`
Claude Code does. Subagent models are pinned per agent by
`ZCODE_AGENT_MODELS` in `bin/craft-sync-codex`; an agent missing from that
map inherits the session default model.

## Ownership

Never edit a `*.human.md` file. Report the fragment and its location instead,
and let a human place it.
